items.title: Left Atrial Stiffness Index and Prognosis Across Heart Failure Phenotypes in Acute Heart Failure: Insights from the STRATS-AHF Registry.
items.abstract: The left atrial stiffness index (LASI), calculated as mitral E/e' divided by LA reservoir strain, reflects atrial myopathy and elevated filling pressure but has been studied mainly in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). We examined whether LASI predicts all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization, and adds to established risk factors, across HF phenotypes in acute heart failure (AHF). We analyzed 3,133 patients with AHF from the multicenter STRATS-AHF registry, classified by LVEF into HFrEF, HFmrEF, and HFpEF. During a median follow-up of 32.5 months, 616 (19.7%) had HF admissions, and 1,281 (40.9%) died. After adjustment, each doubling of LASI was associated with mortality (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.08-1.19), as was LASI above the exploratory cutoff of 1.0 (HR 1.27, 95% CI 1.11-1.46). The association was similar across phenotypes (P for interaction = 0.65) and extended to HF hospitalization and the composite of death or HF hospitalization. LASI added modestly to established predictors; after adjustment for NT-proBNP, its association was not significant in patients with a measured value (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.97-1.10) but persisted after multiple imputation in the whole cohort (HR 1.10, 95% CI 1.04-1.15). In patients hospitalized for AHF, a higher LASI independently predicted all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization across HF phenotypes. Obtained from the admission echocardiogram, LASI captures an atrial component of risk that LVEF does not reflect, although part of this information overlaps with that of NT-proBNP; whether it can guide management remains to be tested.

items.title: Dual Pathway Modulation with SGLT2 Inhibitors and Aldosterone Synthase Inhibitors in Cardio-Kidney Disease: Rationale and Trial Design of the EASi Program.
items.abstract: Cardio-kidney diseases share interconnected pathophysiology where renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) overactivation drives pathologic hemodynamic, neurohormonal, inflammatory, and fibrotic changes leading to progressive cardiac and kidney dysfunction. Current RAAS-modulating therapies are limited by residual RAAS risk and aldosterone breakthrough despite angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker therapy, incomplete blockade of aldosterone with mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) antagonists, hyperkalemia, and suboptimal implementation. Aldosterone synthase inhibitors (ASi) act upstream of the MR to lower aldosterone production, modulating both MR-dependent and MR-independent aldosterone effects without competing for receptor occupancy. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) reduce adverse cardiovascular and kidney events through cellular, hemodynamic and metabolic effects. The complementary mechanisms of SGLT2i/ASi (SASi) may provide improved cardio-kidney protection. The EASi program will determine whether SASi therapy, added to background guideline-directed therapy including an ACE inhibitor, ARB, or ARNI as appropriate, can improve cardiovascular and kidney outcomes beyond SGLT2 inhibitor monotherapy. EASi-PROTKT (∼11,800 participants) evaluates prevention of incident heart failure events or cardiovascular death in patients with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and established cardiovascular disease. EASi-HF Preserved (∼6,000) and EASi-HF Reduced (∼4,200) evaluate cardiovascular death and first heart failure events across the LVEF spectrum. EASi-KIDNEY (∼11,000) evaluates kidney disease progression and cardiovascular endpoints in chronic kidney disease patients with and without type 2 diabetes. EASi-SYNC (∼500) is a Phase 2 trial comparing SASi versus staggered initiation of SGLT2i and ASi in patients with CKD. Together, these trials will enroll >33,000 participants and test whether SASi can redefine standard of care across the cardio-kidney disease spectrum.

items.title: Global reporting of Brugada syndrome in VigiBase®: A disproportionality analysis.
items.abstract: Brugada syndrome (BrS) represents a rare but potentially malignant cardiac channelopathy, which may be precipitated by drugs, although data mainly derive from case reports/series. To describe the global reporting of BrS with drugs, including co-occurrence patterns, and identify novel potential associations. We used VigiBase® to perform descriptive and disproportionality analyses. The reporting odds ratio (ROR) and Bayesian information component (IC) with relevant 95% confidence/credibility intervals (95% CI) were used as disproportionality measures to identify signals of disproportionate reporting (SDR). We performed a network analysis to assess the co-occurrence patterns of related medications based on Jaccard similarity. We included 544 deduplicated cases of BrS (94.7% serious events, 30.9% females, median time to onset of 30 days, 40.8% physician-reported, 63% from North America), with bupropion (n = 50), nortriptyline (n = 40) and flecainide (n = 34) as most frequently reported suspected drugs. Among 39 drugs with at least four reports, 32 emerged with an SDR, of which 17 were not listed in the BrS website (http://www.brugadadrugs.org), such as clozapine and loperamide (often overdosed). The co-occurrence network included 17 medications, regardless of the labelled role (suspected, interacting or concomitant), with a total of 12 potential co-occurrences; fentanyl exhibited the highest closeness centrality (1.0), whereas the strongest co-occurrence was reported between bupropion and nortriptyline (Jaccard similarity of 0.31). Notwithstanding limitations related to pharmacovigilance and the complex BrS pathophysiology, we identified 32 medications with over-reporting of BrS, including 17 drugs not listed in the BrS website as well as clusters in affective disorders and anaesthesia.

items.title: Very Early-Onset Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Complicated by an Aorto-Left Atrial Fistula and Aortic Root Pseudoaneurysm.
items.abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis. Infective endocarditis (IE) is an uncommon but potentially devastating complication, typically presenting weeks to months after valve implantation. Very early-onset prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE), occurring within 48 hours of implantation, poses a particular diagnostic challenge, as infectious complications must be distinguished from procedure-related structural injury and sterile postprocedural inflammatory changes. We report the case of an 81-year-old man who underwent transfemoral TAVI with a self-expanding Evolut FX valve for severe symptomatic aortic stenosis. The procedure was uneventful, with satisfactory immediate angiographic and echocardiographic findings. Within 48 hours, the patient developed fever and elevated inflammatory markers. Two independent blood culture sets were positive for methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA). Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG-PET/CT) demonstrated increased metabolic uptake at the aortic root. Given the early postprocedural timing, this finding was interpreted cautiously, as sterile inflammatory changes could not be excluded. Subsequent transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) revealed a prosthetic valve vegetation, an aortic-root pseudoaneurysm, and an aorto-left atrial fistula with continuous shunt flow. The combination of microbiological and echocardiographic findings fulfilled the diagnostic criteria for definite prosthetic valve IE. Surgical intervention was considered prohibitive by the multidisciplinary Heart Team, and antimicrobial treatment was administered. Despite treatment, the patient's clinical condition rapidly deteriorated, resulting in death within one week of diagnosis. This case highlights the importance of integrating clinical and microbiological findings with multimodality imaging in diagnosing very early-onset PVE, while carefully considering potential procedure-related structural injury.

items.title: Salmonella enterica-Associated Myopericarditis Following Acute Gastroenteritis.
items.abstract: A previously healthy man in his early 20s presented with several days of febrile gastroenteritis, followed by acute pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea. Initial evaluation demonstrated markedly elevated cardiac biomarkers and inflammatory markers, electrocardiogram changes consistent with acute pericarditis, and preserved left ventricular systolic function on transthoracic echocardiogram. Stool polymerase chain reaction testing and blood cultures identified Salmonella enterica . A clinical diagnosis of suspected Salmonella -associated myopericarditis was made, although direct myocardial infection could not be confirmed. The patient was treated with targeted antimicrobial therapy in addition to anti-inflammatory therapy with aspirin and colchicine. His gastrointestinal and cardiac symptoms resolved rapidly, and he was discharged in stable condition with activity restriction and cardiology follow-up. This case highlights a rare but potentially life-threatening cardiac complication associated with non-typhoidal Salmonella infection in a young, otherwise healthy adult and underscores the importance of maintaining diagnostic vigilance when gastrointestinal prodromes precede acute chest pain with myocardial injury.

items.title: Guillain-Barré/Miller Fisher Overlap Syndrome Associated With Listeria monocytogenes Peritonitis During Chemotherapy for Ovarian Cancer: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Guillain-Barré/Miller Fisher overlap syndrome (GBS/MFS overlap syndrome) is an acute immune-mediated polyneuropathy characterized by features of Miller Fisher syndrome, including ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and decreased tendon reflexes, accompanied by limb weakness. We report a case of clinically diagnosed GBS/MFS overlap syndrome occurring in association with Listeria monocytogenes peritonitis during chemotherapy for high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC). A 62-year-old woman developed fever, diplopia, distal sensory disturbance, lower-extremity weakness, and ataxia 13 days after receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Neurological examination revealed abducens nerve palsy and decreased deep tendon reflexes. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed no abnormalities, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed no pleocytosis or elevated protein level. Nerve conduction studies showed reduced compound muscle action potential and sensory nerve action potential amplitudes. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed encapsulated ascites, and ascitic fluid culture was positive for L. monocytogenes. Her neurological symptoms gradually improved following antibiotic therapy and drainage of the ascites without specific immunotherapy. Although anti-GQ1b antibody testing was not performed, the combination of MFS-like features, limb weakness, and electrophysiological evidence of motor-sensory polyneuropathy was most consistent with a clinical diagnosis of GBS/MFS overlap syndrome. The temporal association suggests a possible relationship among infection, malignancy, and immune-mediated neuropathy; however, their respective contributions and a causal relationship with L. monocytogenes infection could not be established.
items.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research

items.title: Engineering Theranostic Nanomedicines for Clinical Translation: Nano-Bio Interactions, Responsive Design, Multimodal Function, and Scale-Up.
items.abstract: Theranostic nanomedicines are engineered multifunctional systems that integrate diagnostic sensing, imaging, and therapeutic delivery within a single nanoscale platform. Their performance depends not only on material composition but also on controllable nano-bio interactions, transport, targeting, stimulus responsiveness, and manufacturability. This review examines the bioengineering principles underlying next-generation theranostic nanomedicines, including lipid, polymeric, mesoporous silica, inorganic, extracellular-vesicle-derived, and cell-membrane-camouflaged platforms. Particular emphasis is placed on how physicochemical design governs protein-corona formation, circulation, biodistribution, cellular uptake, and clearance, and how endogenous or externally applied stimuli can be engineered for spatiotemporally controlled cargo release and imaging feedback. We further discuss the integration of multimodal imaging with nucleic-acid delivery, CRISPR/Cas gene editing, immunotherapy, ferroptosis, sonodynamic therapy, and photothermal therapy, together with emerging uses of artificial intelligence and machine learning for formulation optimization, image analysis, toxicity prediction, and treatment-response modeling. Despite rapid technological progress, clinical translation remains constrained by heterogeneous biological behavior, limited targeting efficiency, long-term safety uncertainties, complex manufacturing, batch-to-batch variability, and regulatory challenges. Future development should shift from increasingly complex multifunctional constructs toward platforms with measurable design-function relationships, scalable Good Manufacturing Practice-compatible production, standardized characterization, and clinically relevant validation. Such an engineering-focused approach could help advance theranostic nanomedicine from predominantly preclinical multifunctional systems toward reproducible technologies for precision diagnosis and therapy.

items.title: Yellow fever vaccination promotes immunogenicity in children thymectomized due to heart surgery.
items.abstract: Yellow fever is a viral illness that may present a high mortality rate. For live-attenuated 17DD vaccine to be effective, a T-cell-mediated immune response is required. Neonatal cardiac surgeries require total thymectomy that might affect thymus function, and thymus disorders are among the contraindications to yellow fever vaccination. We aimed to determine whether children who underwent thymectomy maintain adequate cellular and humoral immune responses to the yellow fever vaccine compared to age-matched controls with intact thymus. In this case-control study, 26 children who underwent total thymectomy during arterial switch operation for transposition of the great arteries before they were aged 4 months and received at least one dose of yellow fever vaccine were compared to a control group of 27 children. We examined neutrophil counts and the immune response mounted by lymphomononuclear cells in samples stimulated with yellow fever vaccine virus. We assessed the levels of neutralizing antibodies and cytokine expression against yellow fever virus in both thymectomized and control groups. Thymectomized patients had no clinical signs of immunodeficiency. They presented decreased lymphocyte counts and IL-4 and IL-1β expression levels, but similar IL-10 and IFN-γ expression levels as compared to the controls. Antibody titration of serum obtained from patients vaccinated with the live-attenuated yellow fever vaccine did not reveal differences between thymectomized and control groups. Our study shows that children with resected thymus maintain a robust and functional immune response to the 17DD yellow fever vaccine, which supports that vaccinating this population is safe and necessary.
items.journal: Pediatric allergy and immunology : official publication of the European Society of Pediatric Allergy and Immunology

items.title: Immunological Mechanisms in Recurrent Spontaneous Abortion: A Critical Review of Immune-Based Diagnostic and Therapeutic Approaches.
items.abstract: Recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA), commonly defined as two or more pregnancy losses, is a heterogeneous condition involving genetic, anatomical, endocrine, infectious, and immunological factors. Immune dysregulation at the maternal-fetal interface has been associated with pregnancy loss through altered natural killer (NK) cell phenotypes and activity, imbalances among T-cell subsets, abnormal macrophage polarization, autoantibodies, and complement activation. However, the strength of evidence differs substantially across these pathways: many cellular and cytokine findings are associative, vary with tissue source and gestational timing, and have not been established as independent causes or validated clinical tests. This review examines the current evidence linking innate and adaptive immune responses to RSA and considers how these findings inform immunological assessment and treatment. Established clinical approaches, particularly antithrombotic treatment for appropriately diagnosed obstetric antiphospholipid syndrome, are distinguished from candidate biomarkers and investigational immunotherapies, including NK-cell-directed interventions, intravenous immunoglobulin, and lymphocyte immunotherapy. Important limitations include heterogeneous case definitions, non-standardized assays, small or selected study populations, and inconsistent treatment protocols. By integrating mechanistic findings with the quality and clinical applicability of available evidence, this review identifies priorities for standardized biomarker validation, prospective patient stratification, and adequately powered trials.

items.title: Effects of Neoadjuvant Immunochemotherapy on Perioperative Rocuronium Neuromuscular Blockade and Sugammadex Reversal in Elderly Patients with Esophageal Cancer: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NICT) is increasingly used in elderly patients with esophageal cancer, but its effects on neuromuscular blockade and reversal remain unclear. We evaluated NICT effects on rocuronium-induced blockade and sugammadex reversal in elderly esophagectomy patients. This prospective observational cohort study recruited 65 elderly patients (≥65 years) undergoing elective esophagectomy at Jiangsu Cancer Hospital; 57 were analyzed (29 NICT, 28 treatment-naive (TN) group). NICT patients received PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors plus taxanes and platinum; TN patients received no neoadjuvant treatment. Rocuronium 0.6 mg/kg was given as a peripheral intravenous bolus, then infused and titrated by quantitative neuromuscular monitoring. After surgery, when the second train-of-four (TOF) twitch was detectable, both groups received sugammadex 2 mg/kg. The primary outcome was mean consumption rate of rocuronium. Secondary outcomes included rocuronium onset time, times to T1 recovery of 10% and 25%, and recovery index and time to TOF ratio (TOFr) recovery to 90% after sugammadex; adverse events were recorded. Mean consumption rate of rocuronium was higher with NICT (12.73 ± 2.80 vs 10.54 ± 1.56 μg·kg -1 ·min -1 ; mean difference 2.19, 95% CI 0.98-3.40; P<0.001; Hedges'g=0.95, 95% CI 0.40-1.49). Rocuronium onset was longer (4.18 ± 1.73 vs 3.01 ± 0.99 min; P=0.003), and times to T1 recovery of 10% and 25% were shorter (P=0.001 and P<0.001). No significant difference was detected in sugammadex-assisted recovery index (P=0.196) or time to TOFr recovery to 90% (P=0.299); however, the study was not powered for these outcomes, and findings were inconclusive. Adverse events were comparable. In elderly esophagectomy patients, NICT was associated with higher rocuronium requirements, delayed onset, and faster spontaneous recovery, consistent with reduced sensitivity. Its effect on sugammadex reversal remained inconclusive. Quantitative monitoring and individualized titration can manage these changes, but the single-center observational design limits generalization.

items.title: HIV Co-Infection and Hepatic Outcomes in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
items.abstract: MASLD affects roughly one-third of people with HIV (PWH), yet data on advanced hepatic outcomes are limited. We examined the association of HIV co-infection with hepatic outcomes in propensity score-matched adults with MASLD. Using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (~114.6 million patients), we identified adults with MASLD stratified by HIV status, excluding viral hepatitis, alcohol-related and other chronic liver diseases. Patients were 1:1 propensity-matched on demographics, BMI, smoking, cardiometabolic comorbidities, laboratory values and medications, then followed for 5 years (Kaplan-Meier, Cox, competing-risk analyses). Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and a composite hepatic decompensation endpoint (ascites/spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, variceal disease, portal hypertension, hepatic encephalopathy, hepatorenal/hepatopulmonary syndrome or liver transplantation). After matching (6666 per group), HIV-positive patients had a higher risk of the composite hepatic outcome (HR 1.25, 95% CI 1.04-1.50) and lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.62-0.88). Individual outcomes, including cirrhosis (HR 1.32, 95% CI 0.98-1.78), were not statistically significant. Severe immunosuppression (CD4 < 200 cells/μL) more than doubled composite hepatic risk (HR 2.11, 95% CI 1.11-4.00), while ART exposure showed no effect (HR 1.00, 95% CI 0.68-1.48). Descriptive competing-risk analyses (unmatched) showed higher cirrhosis incidence despite lower mortality. After comprehensive metabolic matching, HIV co-infection remained associated with modestly increased composite hepatic decompensation, while individual endpoints such as cirrhosis were attenuated, consistent with residual ascertainment bias from greater healthcare contact. Severe immunosuppression, not ART exposure, identified a high-risk subgroup. These findings support targeted liver surveillance in PWH with MASLD, especially at low CD4 counts. Fatty liver disease caused by metabolic factors (MASLD) is common in people living with HIV, but it is unclear whether HIV worsens liver outcomes. Using a large US health records database, we compared more than 6600 HIV‐positive adults with MASLD to an equal number of HIV‐negative adults matched on demographics, body weight and a comprehensive set of metabolic risk factors and followed them for up to 5 years. HIV‐positive patients had a 25% higher risk of developing serious liver complications overall, and this risk was more than twice as high in those with the weakest immune systems (CD4 counts under 200). Individual complications such as cirrhosis showed a similar direction of effect but were no longer statistically significant once metabolic risk factors were rigorously accounted for. Surprisingly, overall death rates were lower in the HIV‐positive group, probably because they see doctors more regularly as part of their HIV care. These results suggest that people with both HIV and fatty liver disease—especially those with weakened immune systems—should be monitored closely for liver scarring.
items.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

items.title: Development and Internal Validation of an On-Treatment Nomogram for Hepatocellular Carcinoma Prediction in Chinese Patients with Chronic Hepatitis B Receiving Long-Term Nucleos(t)ide Analogue Therapy.
items.abstract: This research was conducted to develop and perform internal statistical validation of a prognostic nomogram specifically designed to predict the individual risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in Chinese adults infected with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) receiving sustained long-term treatment with nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs). In this retrospective observational cohort study, 380 Chinese individuals with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) who had been continuously receiving nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) treatment for at least 36 consecutive months between 2020 and 2022 were recruited. These participants were randomly divided into a model development training set (n=266) and a separate internal performance validation set (n=114). By using a combination of Cox proportional hazards regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regularization, we screened and selected the significant predictive variables, and thus obtained four core independent prognostic factors: chronological age, liver stiffness measurement derived from transient elastography (LSM), quantifiable circulating hepatitis B virus RNA (HBV RNA) and peripheral blood platelet concentration. The prognostic model was then evaluated in three important aspects: discriminative power, calibration accuracy and practical utility in clinical decision-making, comparing its performance with four widely recognized existing risk scoring systems: REACH-B, PAGE-B, modified PAGE-B and LEAST prediction tools. During a median observation period of 4.2 years, 25 out of the enrolled subjects experienced hepatocellular carcinoma. The simplified final prognostic nomogram includes four easily measurable baseline and serial treatment-related variables: age of the patient at the beginning of the study, liver stiffness measured at the 36-month visit, detectable serum hepatitis B virus RNA at the 3-year point, and platelet count at the 3-year period. The obtained predictive model shows good internal discriminative ability with concordance indices of 0.87 in the training subset and 0.85 in the external validation subset. The paired time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves gave area under the curve values of 0.89 and 0.87 for the two groups respectively. Evaluation of model calibration indicates that the predicted and actual risks of hepatocellular carcinoma are well correlated in all risk categories, and decision curve analysis confirms that the tool provides significant net clinical benefit for patients and doctors over a wide range of risk levels from 5% to 35%. In the internal validation cohort, the new nomogram performs significantly better than the existing widely used hepatocellular carcinoma risk assessment methods. A newly established prediction score system for hepatocellular carcinoma, which has been validated internally, includes four important clinical indicators: the patient's age, liver stiffness measurements taken after 36 months of treatment, the measurable amounts of hepatitis B virus RNA at that time, and the platelet counts in the peripheral blood at the 3-year follow-up examination. This predictive model shows good discrimination ability in differentiating the high-risk groups from the normal population within our patient sample. Although the initial findings are positive, there are still three main limitations affecting the practical application of the tool: the small number of hepatocellular carcinoma cases observed during the study period, the assessment of prognostic factors being limited only to the 3-year time point without using a formal landmark analysis to deal with competing risks and varying treatment effects, and the absence of external validation tests in other regions or demographic groups. Before this prediction tool can be used routinely in clinical practice, it is necessary to conduct independent validation studies in numerous institutions with large and various patient groups.

items.title: Immunoinformatic and Structural Design of an Influenza A DNA Vaccine Based on Conserved Nucleoprotein Epitopes and Heat Shock Protein 70 Adjuvant.
items.abstract: Influenza A is a health concern, as it constantly mutates and changes antigens. The conventional vaccine is not very effective in providing immunity. We have designed and characterized a DNA multi-epitope vaccine based on conserved regions of the influenza A nucleoprotein (NP) and have assessed the immune response. This is a bioinformatics study carried out in 2025 at the Pasteur Institute of Iran in Tehran. Epitopes were predicted using the immune epitope database and were screened for conservancy, antigenicity, toxicity, and allergenicity using the alignment-independent antigenicity prediction server (VaxiJen), toxicity prediction tool (ToxinPred), and allergenicity prediction tool (AllergenFP).The vaccine contains a cell-penetrating peptide (CPP) derived from the hemagglutinin protein, a vascular endothelial growth factor 183 (VEGF-183) signal peptide, a tetanus toxoid (TT) helper peptide (830-844), NP peptides, and two repeats of heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70)(407-426). The peptides are arranged using flexible and rigid linkers. The structure was predicted using the self-optimized prediction method with alignment (SOPMA) and AlphaFold2. The structure was further analyzed using high-ambiguity-driven protein-protein docking (HADDOCK) with human leukocyte antigen (HLA) class I and II and toll-like receptor (TLR) 2 and 4, followed by a 200-ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. The docking study showed proper interaction of the selected peptides with HLA and murine BALB/c (H-2d) major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I and II and the whole vaccine with innate immune system receptors. In silico immune simulation indicated cytokine release and T cell activation patterns. The constructed multi-epitope DNA construct was predicted to be antigenic and non-toxic, with structural stability and immunogenic potential. These computational results support prioritizing this construct for experimental expression and murine preclinical validation (immunogenicity, safety, and protection).

items.title: Quantitative Estimation of the Risk of Rift Valley Fever Virus Spread via Legal Livestock Movements From Northeastern KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
items.abstract: Rift Valley fever (RVF) virus (RVFV) is a mosquito-borne zoonotic pathogen with major implications for animal and human health. There have been reports of large RVF outbreaks in the interior of South Africa in the 1950s, the 1970s, and 2010-2011. Northeastern KwaZulu-Natal (KZN), which shares borders with Eswatini and Mozambique, was reported to be a RVF hyperendemic area in 2019, with the detection of RVFV related to the virus responsible for the 1950 outbreak. Frequent livestock movements occur out of this area under permits issued by the state veterinary services. This study aimed to estimate the probability of RVFV being spread from northeastern KZN to a destination elsewhere in South Africa via legal movement of cattle and goats. Specifically, the monthly risk of at least one viraemic animal arriving at a destination outside the study area was estimated. A spatial-stochastic risk assessment model was designed to estimate monthly and location-specific risk of RVFV export, following World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) guidelines. The model was run by integrating data from previous studies on the characterisation of domestic ruminant movement patterns and on livestock RVFV seroprevalence and seroconversion rate in cattle and goats reported from the study area. The animal movement data included animal movement permit records (2015-2018) from the KZN Department of Agriculture and Rural Development (KZNDARD) from 94 dip tanks across three ecological areas (mountain, riverine and coastal). Goats posed the highest probability of contributing to the RVFV spread to a destination location outside the study area. This aligns with their predominance in animal exports across all regions, particularly in the riverine area, which alone accounted for 51.6% of all cattle and goat movements. Temporal modelling showed the peak risk of RVFV viraemic animals arriving at a destination to be during January-March for goats (99%, [2-100] 95% ) and February for cattle (99%, [2-100] 95% ), coinciding with increased animal movements and favourable environmental conditions for vector activity. Mountain areas consistently showed low risk. In contrast, the coastal areas presented moderate but variable risk throughout the year. Sensitivity analysis identified incidence rate of RVFV infection per month, the number of animals exported per month, and the duration of viraemia as the parameters in the model that had a strong effect on the variability in the probability of exporting viraemic animals. There is a high probability of RVFV viraemic animals arriving at destinations elsewhere in South Africa via legal movements from northeastern KZN. The risk was highest from the riverine and coastal areas for cattle and goats, the riverine areas presenting the highest risk of export. The late summer months (February-March) posed the highest threat. Integrating spatiotemporal risk modelling into a One Health surveillance framework could enhance early detection, enable targeted interventions, and reduce the risk of both animal and human RVFV exposure in South Africa. Risk of exposure assessment at arrival is also needed to ultimately estimate the risk of the virus being responsible for outbreaks in other regions of South Africa.

items.title: Conditional Survival of Patients With Liver-Metastatic Gastro-Entero-Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors by Treatment Paradigm: A National Cancer Database Analysis.
items.abstract: Patients with gastro-entero-pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEPNETs) have the potential for prolonged survival; however, how prognosis evolves over time according to surgical treatment remains poorly characterized. We hypothesized that combined primary and distant-site surgery, particularly with negative primary resection margins, would be associated with superior overall and conditional survival, whereas patients receiving less extensive surgical treatment would demonstrate greater improvement in conditional survival over time. The NCDB was queried for patients with synchronous liver-metastatic GEPNETs diagnosed between 2010 and 2021. Patients with no follow-up, functional tumors, and grade 3 according to WHO definitions were excluded. Overall survival (OS) was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards modeling. Five-year conditional survival (CS) was estimated among patients surviving 1-5 years following diagnosis. From 17,943 patients, 15.7% underwent combined primary and distant-site surgery, 23.8% primary resection alone, and 1.9% distant-site surgery alone, and 58.6% underwent neither procedure. Five-year OS was highest following combined surgery (78.0%), compared with primary resection alone (68.6%), distant-site surgery alone (53.3%), and neither procedure (31.4%). Among patients surviving 5 years after diagnosis, the probability of surviving an additional 5 years increased to 74.5% following distant-site surgery alone and 52.2% following neither procedure. Conversely, patients undergoing combined surgery maintained high but modestly declining 5-year CS (78.0% at diagnosis vs. 71.6% conditional on surviving 5 years). Among patients undergoing combined surgery, R0 primary resection was associated with superior 5-year survival compared with R1 resection (81.8% vs. 71.1%), with this advantage persisting across conditioning intervals associated with CS. Patients with synchronous liver-metastatic GEPNETs demonstrate distinct conditional survival trajectories according to surgical treatment strategy. Combined primary and distant-site surgery, particularly with R0 primary resection, is associated with favorable long-term survival. Patients undergoing limited or no surgery experience greater improvement in conditional survival over time. These findings support incorporating conditional survival into individualized prognostic counseling.

items.title: Metastatic Patterns of Cachexia in Advanced Nonsmall Cell Lung Cancer in a National Health System.
items.abstract: Cancer cachexia is a major contributor to morbidity and mortality in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet clinical predictors associated with cachexia at time of metastatic diagnosis remain incompletely understood. Large integrated healthcare systems with longitudinal clinical data provide an opportunity to identify patients at increased risk for cachexia. We evaluated demographic and clinical characteristics associated with cachexia at the time of metastatic diagnosis in a national Veterans Health Administration cohort of patients with metastatic NSCLC. This retrospective national cohort study included 23 292 patients diagnosed with metastatic NSCLC within the Veterans Health Administration from 1 January 2010 to September 30 2025. Following consensus criteria, cachexia was defined as either weight loss of greater than 5% of body weight within 6 months prior to the date of diagnosis or weight loss of greater than 2% within the 6 months prior to the date of diagnosis when body mass index was less than 20 kg/m 2 . Demographic characteristics, comorbidity burden, smoking status, histology and organ-specific metastatic involvement at diagnosis were assessed. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with cachexia, and cox proportional hazards models evaluated associations with overall survival. Among 23 292 patients (median age 69; 97.6% male; 19.4% non-Hispanic Black), cachexia was present at diagnosis in 10 365 (44.5%). Liver metastases (adjusted OR [aOR] 1.22, 95% CI: 1.15-1.30, p  ≥ 7 : aHR: 1.60, 95% CI: 1.49-1.72, p < 0.001) were also independently associated with cachexia. Cachexia predicted worse survival (aHR: 1.40, 95% CI: 1.36-1.44, p < 0.001). Cachexia is highly prevalent at the time of metastatic NSCLC diagnosis and is independently associated with liver and bone metastatic involvement. These findings support the hypothesis that metastatic organotropism contributes to cachexia risk and suggest that organ-specific metastatic patterns may improve identification of patients who could benefit from earlier cachexia screening and intervention.
items.journal: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle

items.title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Rare Cancer Identification: An Ontology-Guided NLP Framework Using Structured Electronic Health Records.
items.abstract: Rare cancers constitute nearly one-quarter of all cancer diagnoses worldwide and pose major challenges due to delayed diagnosis and limited treatment options. However, systematic data on their detection remain limited. Although international classification of diseases, tenth revision (ICD-10) codes provide valuable information regarding the patient's medical history, they lack sufficient detail to identify many rare cancers. This study aimed to develop and validate an ontology-based natural language processing (NLP) pipeline, using the Saudi Real-World Evidence Network (SRWEN) data to improve the detection and classification of rare cancers. This cross-sectional analysis examined electronic health record (EHR) diagnostic descriptions from SRWEN database, covering 2015-2025. The NLP pipeline used SciSpaCy, term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF), and SapBERT to map diagnostic descriptions to concepts from four biomedical references: Orphanet, Orphanet rare disease ontology (ORDO), national cancer institute thesaurus (NCIt), and unified medical language system (UMLS). Two authors manually reviewed all the concepts mapped by the three approaches. Positive predictive value (PPV) was the primary performance measure. Mapping was performed on 45,118 unique diagnostic descriptions against 832 unique rare-cancer concepts. The ICD-10 anchored TF-IDF approach achieved a PPV of 88% (95% CI: 81-93%), while SciSpaCy yielded a PPV of 19% (95% CI: 17-20%), and SapBERT yielded a PPV of 47% (95% CI: 44-51). A total of 4,971 patients were identified with rare cancers (median age = 60 years; IQR = 34 years; 62.0% male). The three most common rare malignancies, grouped by primary organ system, were liver and intrahepatic bile duct cancers (36.6%), brain-related cancers (13.3%), and bronchus and lung cancers (6.9%). Ontology-based NLP greatly improved diagnostic precision of rare cancers using only structured clinical data in EHRs.

items.title: Incidental Metastatic High-Grade Neuroendocrine Carcinoma Diagnosed by Liver Biopsy During Cholecystectomy: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Neuroendocrine neoplasms range from relatively indolent well-differentiated tumors to aggressive poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs). Diagnosis can be challenging when nonspecific symptoms coexist with another disease that provides a plausible explanation for the presentation. A 70-year-old woman developed nausea, vomiting, and epigastric abdominal pain several weeks after pelvic reconstructive surgery. Evaluation demonstrated abnormal liver tests, cholelithiasis, and a heterogeneous nodular liver initially concerning for cirrhosis. Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography showed no choledocholithiasis or significant biliary dilation. She underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy with liver wedge biopsy. Gallbladder pathology confirmed chronic cholecystitis, cholelithiasis, and porcelain gallbladder; unexpectedly, the liver biopsy demonstrated high-grade NEC, small-cell type. Persistent abdominal pain and cholestatic liver abnormalities after cholecystectomy prompted further evaluation. Staging demonstrated extensive hepatic involvement, a right middle-lobe pulmonary lesion, bulky mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy, and multifocal osseous metastatic disease. The overall pattern favored metastatic small-cell NEC of pulmonary origin, although the thoracic disease was not biopsied in the available records. She received carboplatin and etoposide, later with atezolizumab, but developed neutropenia, pneumonia, recurrent hospitalizations, progressive cancer-related pain, weight loss, and worsening metastatic disease. With progressive hepatic and osseous disease, declining functional status, and worsening hepatic dysfunction, she ultimately elected comfort-focused treatment and home hospice. This case demonstrates how an aggressive metastatic malignancy can remain obscured by legitimate concurrent diagnoses. Persistence of findings unexplained by the initial diagnosis and failure to improve as expected after appropriate treatment should prompt diagnostic reassessment.

items.title: [Ablation of tumors - increasing in indications and frequency].
items.abstract: Ablation is a treatment modality that is increasing in indications and frequency. Ablation can replace surgery in certain tumor types, such as liver tumors, with equivalent oncological outcome. Ablation is associated with a low frequency of serious complications. New treatment methods should be studied from a scientific perspective before being introduced into clinical routine.
